title: Measure the integrality gap

blocks.text: A rail operator's depot-upgrade team wants every plan it publishes to carry its integrality gap, so readers can see how close the LP ceiling is to the best plan. Each candidate is a `Project` with a cost and a value ($k) and an optional `parent`, the project it depends on.
Write two functions in `gap.py`. With $`P`$ the projects, $`C`$ those with a parent $`p(c)`$ and $`B`$ the budget, the model is

items: `solve(projects, budget, integer)` builds this model in MathOpt and returns its optimal value: the MILP solved with HiGHS when `integer` is true, the LP relaxation solved with GLOP when it is false.
`integrality_gap(projects, budget)` returns `(lp_bound, optimum, gap)`, where $`\text{gap} = (z_{LP} - z_{IP}) / |z_{IP}|`$.

blocks.text: The tests use budgets that some plan fits, so both solves end `OPTIMAL`. About fifteen lines.

Two pieces of the result come from the section 2 lesson *Your first LP: splitting a maintenance budget across programs*, in its rule *GLOP Solves It: Read the Status, Then the Amounts, Then the Rows*: `result = mathopt.solve(model, solver_type)` returns the result, `result.termination.reason` says how the solve ended (compare it with `mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL`), and `result.objective_value()` is the optimal value. The reference solution returns `objective_value()` directly, since the tests' budgets always end `OPTIMAL`.

cases.says: the LP bound is the relaxation's value from GLOP and the optimum is the MILP's value from HiGHS
the gap divides by the best plan's value, not by the bound
the parent row is x_c <= x_p, so the relaxation cannot fund more of a child than of its parent

origin.section: The Integrality Gap Is the Distance From the LP Bound to the Best Plan

concepts: the integrality gap compares the relaxation's value with the MILP's, as a share of the MILP's
